deities: Vishnu (as Dhopeshwar, in linga form in the same sanctum)

history.dynasty: Shilahara and Yadava (Seuna), on a Chalukya foundation
history.summary: A celebrated 12th-century Shiva temple on the Krishna river bank at Khidrapur (ancient Koppam/Koppad). Construction is said to have begun in the 7th c. under the Chalukyas but was interrupted by wars; it was built by Shilahara kings Gandaraditya, Vijayaditya and Bhoj-II (1109-1178 AD) and renovated by the Yadava king Singhana II (inscription of 1214-15 AD near the southern door). The four interconnected sections are the Swarga Mandap (round hall with an open-to-sky circular ceiling, 48 uniquely carved pillars), the Sabha Mandap with Mahabharata/Ramayana carvings, the Antaral and the sanctum. Unusual features: devotees first see Vishnu as Dhopeshwar in linga form before the Kopeshwar linga in the same sanctum, and there is no Nandi. 'Kop' means anger - the temple is tied to the legend of Shiva's fury after Sati's self-immolation. Invaders (Aurangzeb, Adilshahi rulers) mutilated the sculptures, including 92 of 96 elephant trunks in the Gajapatta; now ASI-protected.

name: Kopeshwar Temple
town_description: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the row said 'Kolhapur' but the temple is at Khidrapur village, Shirol taluka, Kolhapur district - ~57-58 km east of Kolhapur city, on the Krishna river bank near the Kolhapur-Sangli district border (Narsobachi Wadi is ~15 km away). Note: CSV row 625 'Kopeshwar Temple [Sangli]' is almost certainly a duplicate of this same temple (it is also commonly reached via Sangli/Miraj, which borders Khidrapur) - recommend dedup, do NOT treat as a separate temple.

travel.railway: Kolhapur Junction (~58 km) or Miraj Junction (nearest on the Sangli side)
travel.road: Via Kurundwad (18 km away): Kolhapur-Kurundwad-Khidrapur buses, though infrequent; taxi from Kolhapur (~1.5 hrs); no hotels at Khidrapur - stay at Kolhapur

visitor_information.best_time: Any time of year; monsoon is prettiest, mornings are quietest; avoid peak crowds on Mahashivratri and Shravan Mondays
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily (free entry). Opening-hour conflict: some listings report 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM or 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM (verify)
